# Model Evaluation Report

**Task:** regression — predict `TARGET(PRICE_IN_LACS)` (₹ lakh) from 20 engineered property/location features. R² here is the coefficient of determination for regression, not accuracy.
**Generated by:** `ml/model_comparison.py` from executed runs (`experiment_results.csv`, `model_metrics.json`). No number in this report was typed by hand.

## Protocol

- Input: previous stage's model-ready dataset (28,622 rows). Duplicates investigated first: 567 extra feature-identical rows in 514 groups, 112 of them with conflicting prices (label noise).
- Split: grouped 70/15/15 by feature signature (no signature in two partitions — overlaps: train∩valid 0, train∩test 0) -> train 20,037, validation 4,301, test 4,284.
- All models trained on log1p(target); metrics back-transformed to ₹ lakh. Tuning: seeded random search on validation RMSE with early stopping (boosting). Test scored exactly once, after selection.
- Caveat: engineered frequency/centroid/cluster statistics were fitted (unsupervised, target-free) by the preprocessing stage on its own train split; encoders here were refit on this stage's train only. The unseen-locality experiment below is the strict generalisation check.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linear | 0.5753 | ₹125.54L | — | — | 0.4776 ± 0.0588 |
| Random Forest | 0.7537 | ₹95.60L | 0.7815 | ₹90.04L | 0.7384 ± 0.0395 |
| CatBoost | 0.8028 | ₹85.54L | 0.8305 | ₹79.31L | 0.7966 ± 0.0554 |

| LightGBM | 0.8075 | ₹84.52L | 0.8313 | ₹79.11L | 0.8286 ± 0.0566 |

## Selection

**Winner: XGBoost** (tuned configuration) — lowest validation RMSE under the pre-fixed rule (lowest validation RMSE; near-tie (<0.5%) broken by grouped-CV stability). It was selected on validation + CV evidence, not because of its algorithm family.

## Test — scored once, after selection

| R² | MAE | RMSE | MAPE | SMAPE | Median AE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.7368 | ₹21.71L | ₹75.16L | 28.4% | 19.7% | ₹8.09L |

## Geographic generalisation (unseen localities)

Refit on 80% of localities, scored on 1156 never-seen localities (5,403 rows): **R² 0.6056**, MAE ₹36.14L, RMSE ₹173.68L. The drop vs the random-split test is the honest cost of valuing properties in new places with locality-level location data.

## On the R² 0.96 target

The target was investigated, not assumed. Best measured test R² is **0.7368**. The remaining gap is explained by evidence from the EDA stage: conflicting prices for identical feature vectors, missing price-driving attributes (bathrooms, age, furnishing), locality-level coordinates, and residual field errors. No legitimate preprocessing or tuning choice available on this dataset closes it; claiming 0.96 would require fabricating results.

## Why the winner won

See the validation table: the winner combines the lowest validation RMSE with grouped-CV stability. Gradient boosting fits this data's profile — strong monotone area/BHK effects, high-cardinality location signals, and heavy-tailed prices handled on the log scale — while the linear baseline cannot represent the interactions, and Random Forest's piecewise-constant predictions are coarser at the price extremes. Per-model detail, all trials and failures: `ml/experiment_results.csv`.
